businessObjectives.text: Reduce unplanned downtime without overwhelming maintenance teams with low-value alerts.

requirements.text: The service must score rolling vibration and temperature windows against machine-specific baselines.
Every material anomaly must include machine identity, signal, observed value, baseline, confidence, and explanation.

acceptanceEvidence.text: Given the approved bearing-fault replay set, when anomaly scoring runs, then detection recall is at least 90% and false-alert rate remains below 5%.
Given normal warm-up behavior, when temperature rises within the approved envelope, then no maintenance recommendation is emitted.

completionCriteria.text: Model versioning, replay validation, production monitoring, rollback, and reliability-engineer acceptance are complete.

risks.cause: The labeled bearing-fault dataset covers only two CNC machine models.
risks.effect: The initial model may overstate confidence for other machines.
risks.mitigation: Use model-specific confidence thresholds and shadow evaluation until sufficient labeled data is available.

openQuestions: Which additional machine models must pass replay validation before production rollout?

assessment.summary: The outcome, anomaly contract, replay evidence, ownership, and completion controls are clear. Readiness is reduced by the unresolved production rollout scope for machine models without labeled fault data.

factors.rationale: The downtime-reduction outcome and false-alert constraint establish clear operational intent.
Signals, scoring context, explanation fields, and model-specific behavior are explicitly required.
Replay thresholds and completion controls cover quality, monitoring, rollback, and operational acceptance.
The owning team, disciplines, sprint, priority, and estimate provide actionable planning context.
The limited labeled dataset is visible with a mitigation, but the rollout decision remains unresolved.

recommendations: Agree the production rollout machine-model set and record the reliability owner for each acceptance decision.
Attach shadow-scoring evidence for unsupported machine models before enabling automated maintenance recommendations.

notes.text: As a reliability engineer, I need explainable anomaly detection across vibration and temperature signals so that maintenance can act before equipment fails.
The bearing-fault replay set and normal warm-up examples are available for model validation.
The current model meets recall on the two labeled CNC models; shadow scoring is enabled for the remaining fleet.
Keep the rollout scope explicit and attach the reliability-engineer approval before refinement closes.
